  • If assessed value tops $1,000, a certified letter follows.
  • A certified letter returned unsigned triggers another first class letter, to the owner and any occupant.
  • Right up to the sale, you can clear the tax, penalty, interest and costs at the collector's office.

A notice that never reached you doesn't wipe out the tax. Moved recently? Give the Collector your new mailing address, since notices go to the owner of record.

How to challenge an assessment

Go first to the Assessor, Suite 1 at 204 High Street. The office values property annually and can explain what went into your number. Still disagree? The county Board of Equalization takes filings until the second Monday in July.

The state level is the Missouri State Tax Commission. RSMo 138.430 opens the next level, the Missouri State Tax Commission. Filing is due within the statutory time or 30 days after the board acts, whichever is later, and can be done online, by email, or by post to PO Box 146, Jefferson City, MO 65102. An attorney must file for any corporation, LLC, trust or estate.

You can contest value and still beat the payment deadline by paying under protest. Send the full amount by December 31 on a marked check, with a written statement for the Collector giving your claimed market value.

Bring the tax bill into the price talk early. Tax stays with the land, so whatever is unpaid passes to the buyer. The title company will usually run a tax search, but you can avoid surprises by phoning the Collector yourself to ask the balance and whether an earlier year is open.

If you close in the fall, buyer and seller must decide who pays the bill that lands shortly before December 31. Write the answer into the contract, and ask the title company to hold the seller's share if no bill exists yet. Whoever pays should keep the receipt.

Questions to ask the Collector

One short call to 573-238-1900 now prevents trouble later.

  • Which mailing address is on file?
  • Which payment types do you take, and what does each cost?
  • Has the parcel ever appeared on the August sale list?

Write down the answers and give them to the title company. A bill that is wrong because of value is the Assessor's problem to solve, not the Collector's.

What happens at closing

On closing day the title company works from the balance the Collector gave you. If anything is owed for an earlier year, it comes out of your proceeds first, and the deed goes to the Recorder in Suite 7 after the papers are signed. Because the Recorder keeps the deed record, a clean filing is what puts the buyer's name on the books.

In a rural county with few sales, one open tax year can slow things down, since the buyer and the title company will want proof that nothing is headed for the August sale. Having your payment receipts and the Collector's written balance in hand answers that question quickly.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the tax payoff and the deed filing are often the only steps left once both sides sign. That makes it more important to settle any balance and address problems before the contract date.

December 31, the same as the rest of the state. Call 573-238-1900 and ask for the Collector to learn how and where to pay.

At 204 High Street, Suite 1, Marble Hill, MO 63764. The main number is 573-238-1900, extension 1 for the Assessor.

The fourth Monday in August under state law, every year.

Offices and phone numbers

Everything runs through the courthouse, 102 E Broadway, Bolivar, MO 65613. The Collector is in Suite 6, (417) 326-4032. The Assessor is in Room 9, with the appraiser line at (417) 326-4346 and personal property at (417) 326-4643. The County Clerk is in Suite 11, (417) 326-4031.

Weekday hours are posted as 8 to 4, though one line shows 8 to 5, so call before a long drive. The collector's office handles more than $24 million a year for schools, roads, general revenue and other districts.

Polk County at a glance

Polk County sits in southwest Missouri, in the Springfield metro area, with Bolivar as the county seat. The assessor counts over 18,000 parcels of real estate. Population is 33,604 across 13,760 housing units, and 71.6 percent of occupied homes are owner-lived. The middle owned home is worth $205,800. The county issued 61 building permits in 2025, so new construction adds a little supply each year but not much.

Tax statements and the penalty date

Bills are typically mailed in early November. When a bill goes missing, ask the collector for a copy. The tax is owed either way. A payment postmarked after December 31 draws a penalty.

The office takes no partial payments and will not accept an incorrect amount. You can pay the personal property bill and the real estate bill on different days. Back taxes from earlier years, though, have to be settled first. Online payment runs through a link on the collector's page, where you can also look up paid status for real and personal accounts.

Who pays when a house is sold

The owner of record is responsible for all taxes due on real property, and Missouri law makes no provision for pro-rating a tax bill. So the split between buyer and seller is worked out by the closing agent on the settlement statement. The county plays no part. Personal property follows ownership on January 1. A truck you sell in March still lands on that year's statement.

Owners are also expected to check that the parcel is described correctly and to give the assessor an updated mailing address. The collector cannot change a valuation without the assessor.

How the assessor values property

Values are set as of January 1. Full reassessment of real property comes in odd-numbered years, while new construction is added annually. Assessment ratios run 19 percent of market value on residential land and homes, 32 percent on commercial and other, and 12 percent on agricultural. Cars, trucks, boats and campers are assessed at 33.33 percent, farm equipment and livestock at 12 percent, and historic vehicles at 5 percent.

Notices of increased value are mailed in the first week of June, which is when to start gathering evidence. Staff do exterior inspections only, carry photo identification and leave a card when nobody is home. They may not go inside a structure without permission. The assessor does not set the levy. Each taxing district, such as schools, fire, roads, cities, ambulance and hospitals, sets its own.

How to appeal your assessment

There are three levels, and each has its own date.

Delinquent land tax sale

The collector conducts the auction at the courthouse, 10:00 a.m., fourth Monday in August. The parcel list is published in the Bolivar newspaper for three consecutive weeks beforehand. Paying everything owed ahead of the auction stops it for that parcel. Opening bids equal the taxes, penalties and sale costs. Bidders attend in person and sign an affidavit that they owe no delinquent Missouri tax. Many sellers never reach this point, because a payment before the sale ends it.

  • The buyer receives a Certificate of Purchase, held for one year or until redeemed.
  • The former owner has one year to buy the property back, paying the certificate amount plus 10 percent annual interest on the tax.
  • Later years' taxes paid by the buyer carry 8 percent annual interest.
  • Give the collector at least three business days' notice before redeeming, and allow about twenty minutes.

When nobody redeems, the certificate holder can ask for a Collector's Deed, but only after certified-mail notices go out at least ninety days ahead. The certificate becomes void if the requirements are not met by two years after the sale.

Selling with taxes owed

If your parcel is on the sale list, call the collector first. Ask for the exact payoff, including penalty, interest and costs, and ask how the office wants the money delivered. A written figure helps, because the closing office will request one. If you plan to list the house instead, tell your agent about the delinquent status early so the payoff is built into the timeline. Earlier delinquent years come before the current one, and a title company will want that whole history cleared before closing.

A traditional listing needs repairs, showings and a buyer's lender, and all of that takes time you may not have before the August sale. A cash sale can close faster, with the back taxes paid from your proceeds at the closing table. If the parcel has already sold at auction, the one-year redemption window is the deadline that matters, and the payoff figure must come from the collector. Take the parcel number and ID to the window, and hold on to each receipt for your closing folder.

Credits that lower a bill

The state Property Tax Credit claim, Form 948, is for people who may qualify for a credit or refund. Qualifying seniors and 100 percent disabled individuals can claim up to $750 as renters or $1,100 as owner-occupants, depending on tax or rent paid and household income. For county-level programs beyond that, ask the County Clerk at (417) 326-4031 or the collector at (417) 326-4032.

Anything postmarked after December 31 is penalized. Bills normally arrive in early November.

Can I make a partial payment on a Polk County tax bill?

No. The Collector in Bolivar takes no partial payments and will not accept an incorrect amount. Real estate and personal property can be paid on separate days, with older delinquent years first.

When is the Polk County tax sale?

The fourth Monday in August, 10:00 a.m., at the courthouse. Pay the Collector the tax, penalty, interest and costs before then and the parcel comes off the list.

How long can I redeem a Polk County property sold for taxes?

One year from the sale date. Redemption costs the Certificate of Purchase amount plus 10 percent annual interest, plus 8 percent on any later taxes the buyer paid.

Where do I file a Polk County assessment appeal?

Start with the Assessor's appraiser at (417) 326-4346 before June 30, then use the County Clerk's Board of Equalization form. The State Tax Commission comes last, due August 15 or thirty days after the board's decision, whichever falls later.

Who values and who bills property in Webster County?

In Webster County one office sets the value and another sends the bill. The Assessor sits in Room 19 of the Marshfield courthouse at 417-859-2169, and the Collector sits in Room 15 at 417-859-2683. Mail for the Collector goes to P.O. Box 288, Marshfield, MO 65706.

The Assessor's page describes the task as putting fair market value on property as of the tax date. Two bodies can review that work: the county Board of Equalization and the Missouri State Tax Commission. The page links online personal property filing and a county GIS map. GIS access is a paid subscription arranged by phone.

Rates are a separate matter. Each taxing body adopts its own, and the county's Taxes page shows 2025 rates by school district.

When does a Webster County tax bill come due?

Webster County bills go out in November and are payable as soon as they arrive. December 31 is the cutoff. A check bearing that day's postmark or earlier is on time, while a later one is returned unless the late charges are enclosed.

Anyone paying late follows the schedule printed on the lower part of the statement. Under state law the postmark date is the payment date, and registered or certified mail uses its certification date instead.

How are Webster County homes valued for tax?

Missouri taxes residences on 19 percent of market value. Marshfield's own page repeats that figure along with 32 percent for commercial and industrial property, and says the county does the assessing and collecting for the city.

New real estate values are set in odd-numbered years and stay in place the following year except for new construction. That puts the next general reset on January 1, 2027. A planned increase above 15 percent on a house, improvements aside, calls for a visit to the property. Driving past does not meet the requirement, and the owner has no less than 30 days after the written notice to request an interior look.

How do you contest a Webster County assessment?

Phone the Assessor at 417-859-2169 once a change notice lands, and ask how to set a hearing. The Board of Equalization comes first. Should the Board hold its number, the State Tax Commission is next, with a filing window of 30 days after the Board acts or the chapter's own date if that is later.

Payment need not wait. An owner who settles the entire current bill ahead of delinquency may give the Collector a written protest, and the disputed portion is parked in a separate account. That protest dies unless the owner sues the Collector in circuit court inside 90 days. A person with a timely Commission appeal pending skips the lawsuit, and a winning taxpayer receives the interest the fund earned.

The Assessor's page describes the State Tax Commission as the state agency with general supervision over assessors and the job of enforcing property tax law. Is a senior tax freeze open in Webster County?

The 2026 application window for the senior citizens' property tax credit ran May 1 to June 30, 2026, so it has closed. Applicants had to be 62 before January 1, 2026, and the credit reaches residential real estate tax on a primary home. It holds the bill at 2026 base year levels. It is a freeze, and it does not exempt anything.

Two kinds of tax stay outside it: levies the state constitution guarantees, such as the blind fund and general obligation bonds, and voter-approved increases adopted after the base year. Vehicle tax and other personal property tax are excluded too. Forms were taken at the County Clerk's office in Room 12, with photo identification, a utility bill or voter card as proof of residency, and last year's paid receipt. The Clerk's line is 417-859-8683. Ask the Clerk when the next window opens, and what a mid-year sale does to an approved freeze.

What does the Marshfield city levy add to a bill?

Marshfield property owners pay the city's levy on top of the school, county and special district rates. After voters approve general obligation bonds, the Board of Aldermen sets a debt service rate high enough to cover principal and interest. The parks and cemetery levy has a ceiling that only voters can lift. That ceiling lets collections rise by 5 percent or the Consumer Price Index, whichever is lower, against the prior year.

The county Taxes page breaks its 2025 rate tables into Diggins, Fordland, Marshfield, Niangua, Rogersville, Seymour and Strafford school districts, plus rural Webster County. Match the district printed on your statement, not the mailing city.

  • On the Collector's website by e-check, debit or credit card, where cards add a convenience fee.
  • Accepted forms: cash, personal check, money order, cashier's check. One check can pay several bills.

The Collector says it is not responsible if you pay tax on property that belongs to someone else or skip a parcel you own, so check the account number against your parcel. A statement that never reached you does not erase the tax, penalty or interest.

What do Census figures say about Webster County households?

Webster County counted 36,202 people in the 2010 census and 39,085 in 2020. The 2020 to 2024 survey counts 13,964 households and finds 87.6 percent of residents in the same house a year before. The county is home to 2,990 veterans.

Owners occupy 77.4 percent of occupied homes, the lowest share of Stone, Warren and Webster, so renters have a larger presence here. Landlords get their statements in November like other owners and face the same December 31 postmark date.

The county is part of the Springfield metropolitan area. Six cities (Fordland, Marshfield, Niangua, Rogersville, Seymour and Strafford) and the village of Diggins make up its municipalities. Marshfield, at 1,490 feet, is the state's highest county seat, and its courthouse of Carthage marble dates from 1939 to 1941.

After December 31. Each statement is payable on arrival, and mail needs a postmark dated on or before the 31st.

Where is the Webster County Collector located?

Room 15 of the courthouse, 101 S. Crittenden Street, Marshfield. Mail goes to P.O. Box 288, and the phone is 417-859-2683.

Can I pay a Webster County bill by card?

Yes. The Collector's site takes cards, e-checks and debit, and card payments add a convenience fee.

Is the Webster County senior freeze accepting applications?

Not now. The 2026 window ended June 30, 2026. The County Clerk at 417-859-8683 can say when the next opens.

Who decides Webster County tax rates?

Each taxing body does, meaning schools, cities, fire districts and the county. The Assessor and Collector do not.
